correctness.rationale: PASS: For the line graph L(K_n), a target edge is disjoint from every initially active base edge exactly when both endpoints are outside U(S), giving the literal self-inclusive F(S)=E([n]\U(S)). The case |U|>=n-1 maps to empty; 2<=|U|<=n-2 maps to complementary complete-edge set, then back, so F³=F and no fixed point. Unordered complementary vertex sets with both sides>=2 yield 2^(n-1)-n cycles; support-exact labelled graphs are c_m by inclusion–exclusion. Thus the full basin sizes follow. c_n>= (2^(n-2)-1)² c_{n-2}>2c_{n-2} shows strict dominance. Under G(n,1/2), exceptional basins are exactly the union of events two specified isolated vertices, EXCEPT the empty graph; Bonferroni pair/triple/four-isolate probabilities yield C(n,2)2^-(2n-3) and relative error O(n2^-n). Independent literal closed-neighborhood state enumeration n=4,5,6 (33856 states) matched all cycle/basin claims; proofs cover all n.
